A1.justification: Both PDFs present GenCompositor and provide readable methods, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary material. Corresponding content can be matched despite extensive reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original video harmonization and controllable-generation evaluations, component ablations, and a user study with 19 volunteers.

after.justification: V2 retains these empirical results and adds a VACE comparison, a foreground-encoding ablation, dataset composition results, and additional qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: The background-preservation branch, 42 fusion blocks, ERoPE, masked token injection, and luminance augmentation remain unchanged. V2 formalizes existing operations and documents an interface. CLIP encoding is tested as an ablation, not adopted into the proposed model.

E1.justification: VideoComp, HYouTube, and the existing generation evaluation remain. V2 adds qualitative scenarios involving challenging background lighting and sequential insertion of multiple objects with partial occlusion (Figures 19–20). The new VideoComp breakdown describes existing data rather than expanded training coverage.

E2.justification: VACE joins Tora and Revideo in the controllable-generation comparison in Table 2 and Figure 7. Harmonizer and VideoTripletTransformer, abbreviated VTT in v2, remain the harmonization comparators. The user-study comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 adds FVD and KVD to the four existing VBench metrics while retaining 40 video sets. Appendix G introduces a control replacing VAE foreground encoding with CLIP encoding within the cross-attention ablation. Existing model settings and user-study sample sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a focused CLIP-versus-VAE encoding ablation, descriptive VideoComp composition analysis, and lighting/occlusion case studies. The original four component ablations, ERoPE-axis loss curves, inpainting examples, and trajectory/scale analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. User-study aggregation is unchanged. The added dataset percentages are descriptive results rather than a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 3, the original four metrics in Table 2, and user-study percentages remain unchanged. Table 2 adds VACE results and FVD/KVD scores, including 535.71/45.91 for GenCompositor. Dataset frequencies and qualitative encoding, lighting, and occlusion findings supplement the retained results.

T1.justification: V1 explains ERoPE through positional labels and diagrams. V2 Section 4.4 adds a derivation of attention under stream-specific positional offsets, particularly Equations 8–9. This is a limited mathematical addition supporting the existing procedure; the training objective remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: generative video compositing, the GenCompositor architecture, ERoPE, VideoComp, and superiority over related solutions. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix G adds an explanation linking CLIP-encoding failure to abstract semantic features and their mismatch with VAE features. Appendix J qualifies the retained lighting and occlusion limitations with successful examples and adds discussion of scale-based depth effects and future novel-view/orientation control.

D1.justification: V2 specifies Gaussian smoothing and thresholding for mask inflation and documents the web interface, including its default scale of 0.4. Appendix A newly reports anonymous supplementary code, omitted weights, and planned code/model/data releases. Actual resource availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including VACE, FVD, VBench-2.0, ToonComposer, and OmniDrag, alongside additional background citations. The overall positioning relative to video editing and harmonization remains stable. Publication and citation-format updates do not constitute new research positioning.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact, with localized rewriting and expanded explanations. V2 adds a contents page and statements, converts the numbered supplement to lettered appendices, and incorporates the earlier future-work passage into an expanded discussion.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation, substantially resizing and relocating figures and tables. Table 2 expands, Figure 7 gains VACE examples, and new Figures 10, 15, and 19–21 display dataset composition, an encoding ablation, additional cases, and the interface.

improvement.justification: The ERoPE derivation and added VACE and CLIP-encoding comparisons make the existing technical contribution better supported and easier to assess. The gains are incremental, with principal results retained. A countervailing defect is introduced in Appendix A: its claim of no human subjects conflicts with the retained 19-volunteer study in Appendix E.
